objective: Al terminar usas cláusulas de participio (-ing, -ed y having + participio) para unir ideas de forma concisa en escritura narrativa y formal.

warmup.prompt_es: 'Habiendo terminado, se fue.' 'Rodeado de gente, se sintió solo.' Las cláusulas de participio resumen dos acciones en una frase elegante, muy habitual en textos descriptivos y narrativos.

text: Having finished his novel, the author took a long holiday. Walking along the beach one morning, he noticed an old man painting. Intrigued, he stopped to watch. The painter, dressed in a faded blue shirt, was working on a seascape. Not wanting to disturb him, the author stayed silent.

After a while, the old man turned around. 'Fascinated by the sea?' he asked. 'Yes,' said the author, 'but I can't paint.' 'Neither could I at your age,' the man laughed. 'Encouraged by a teacher, I started at forty.'

The two men became friends. Inspired by their conversations, the author began a new book. Written in only six months, it became a bestseller. Having read it, the painter said, 'You've captured the sea better than I ever did.'

Looking back, the author often wondered whether the book would have existed had he not met the painter. Surrounded by waves and silence, he had found what he had been looking for: a story worth telling.
input.es: Habiendo terminado su novela, el autor se tomó unas largas vacaciones. Paseando por la playa una mañana, se fijó en un anciano que pintaba. Intrigado, se detuvo a mirar. El pintor, vestido con una camisa azul desteñida, trabajaba en una marina. Sin querer molestarlo, el autor guardó silencio. Al cabo de un rato, el anciano se dio la vuelta. '¿Fascinado por el mar?', preguntó. 'Sí', dijo el autor, 'pero no sé pintar'. 'Yo tampoco a su edad', rio el hombre. 'Animado por un profesor, empecé a los cuarenta'. Los dos hombres se hicieron amigos. Inspirado por sus conversaciones, el autor empezó un nuevo libro. Escrito en solo seis meses, se convirtió en un superventas. Habiéndolo leído, el pintor dijo: 'Has captado el mar mejor que yo'. Mirando atrás, el autor se preguntaba a menudo si el libro habría existido de no haber conocido al pintor. Rodeado de olas y silencio, había encontrado lo que buscaba: una historia que valía la pena contar.

md_es: **Cláusulas de participio**
| Tipo | Estructura | Significado | Ejemplo |
| **-ing (activo, simultáneo)** | *V-ing + resto, sujeto + verbo* | dos acciones a la vez o causa | ***Walking** along the beach, he saw a boat.* |
| **Having + participio (anterior)** | *Having + participio, sujeto + verbo* | una acción terminó antes | ***Having finished** his book, he rested.* |
| **-ed (pasivo)** | *participio + resto, sujeto + verbo* | causa o descripción pasiva | ***Inspired** by her, he started painting.* |
| **Having been + participio** | *Having been + participio* | pasiva anterior | ***Having been warned**, they stayed home.* |
| **Negativo** | *Not + V-ing / Not having + participio* | ausencia | ***Not wanting** to disturb him, he left.* |
**Regla clave: mismo sujeto**
- El sujeto implícito de la cláusula de participio es **el mismo** que el de la oración principal.
- ✔ ***Walking** along the beach, **he** noticed an old man.* (él camina y él nota)
- ✘ ***Walking** along the beach, **the sun** was shining.* (el sol no camina) → ✔ *As we were walking along the beach, the sun was shining.*
**Participio como adjetivo reducido (post-modificador)**
- *The man **painting** the boat is my uncle.* = *The man who is painting …*
- *The book **written** by her is a bestseller.* = *The book which was written …*
**Con conjunciones**
- *After finishing, … · Before leaving, … · While walking, … · On arriving, … · Since moving here, … · When asked, …*
**Participio de causa**
- *Being tired, he went to bed.* = *Because he was tired, …* · *Not knowing the answer, she guessed.*
**Errores típicos**
- ✘ *Walking along the beach, the weather was nice.* → ✔ *Walking along the beach, I noticed that the weather was nice.*
- ✘ *Having finish the work, he left.* → ✔ *Having finished the work, he left.*
- ✘ *Inspiring by her, he painted.* → ✔ *Inspired by her, he painted.*
- ✘ *Not to know the answer, she guessed.* → ✔ *Not knowing the answer, she guessed.*
**Ojo:** son frecuentes en escritura formal y narrativa; en habla coloquial se usan menos. Tras una coma, la cláusula de participio suele ir al principio de la frase.
Pronunciación: *intrigued* /ɪnˈtriːɡd/ · *seascape* /ˈsiːskeɪp/ · *encouraged* /ɪnˈkʌrɪdʒd/.
